speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. When did you give birth, and have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge or increased pain in your lower abdomen? Please also let me know if you have had a fever at home and what your highest temperature was.

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or burning sensation when you urinate, and have you noticed any chills or rigors? I would like to assess for signs of infection spreading beyond the uterus. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Culture

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the uterine tenderness and prolonged labor, endometritis is the most likely cause of your fever. I will order blood work to confirm the infection and start antibiotics immediately. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the blood work is normal, I need to rule out other sources of infection or complications like a hematoma or abscess. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite normal labs and ultrasound, your uterine tenderness and fever post-prolonged labor strongly suggest endometritis. I am initiating treatment with broad-spectrum antibiotics to cover the likely polymicrobial infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis
